name: gtx1080ti
description: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (GP102, Pascal, sm_61) at its 1480 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SM; the SM is GP104's (gtx1080).

sources.SM (all core knobs): Inherited from gtx1080: GP102 uses the same Pascal SM as GP104
sources.NUM_CORES: 28 SMs, 3584 CUDA cores (GeForce GTX 1080 Ti specifications)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS: 2.75 MB L2 (11 of GP102's 12 memory controllers and their L2 slices): 22 ways over power-of-two sets
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 352-bit GDDR5X at 11 Gbps (484 GB/s) modelled as the gtx1080's 16 GDDR6 x16 channels at 15125 MT/s: 16 x 2 B x 15.125 GT/s = 484 GB/s, the card's bandwidth
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1480 MHz base clock (1582 MHz boost), base as in gtx1080
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies inherited from gtx1080 (Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1, Tesla P4: the same Pascal SM, L1 and L2 design). Accel-Sim correlates this card (posted hardware runs: pascal-1080ti)
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY: 26 core cycles each way between a core and its dcache, the L1/texture load pipeline, which the dcache bank pipeline (DCACHE_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the None-cycle L1 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 52 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py (after the L1 link) so the SimX pointer chase gives the None-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: Not set: no DRAM latency is published for this part, so dram_cycles is unchecked
